recent_decisions.decision: The leaf tufts were geometrically cubes, and the gate that could see it had to be built before the fix could be judged.

The first instrument grouped cards by PROXIMITY and reported 0.31 against a 0.30 threshold - nearly a false pass. Grouping exactly (one emit_sleeve call is one sleeve) showed the truth: conifer tufts were 100% parallel card pairs, broadleaf tufts 67% perpendicular plus 33% parallel. The golden-angle azimuth fix alone left 33% still near-perpendicular because the normals stayed on one circle; the tilt half is what cleared it, and stratifying those tilts in solid-angle bands (right for POINTS) measured WORSE than no tilt at all, because a sleeve is a set of PLANES. recent_decisions.decision: The canopy parity gate records the level PER SPECIES rather than widening one band.
recent_decisions.why: Broadleaf crowns land on the isotropic leaf-angle kernel almost exactly (0.94-1.05). Fir and pine sit 22% under it at every sun angle, and that is real: a fir carries flat sprays along a branch and the spherify blend pushes its normals horizontal. A single band loose enough to admit 1.30 would stop noticing a broadleaf that broke. The ratio is near-constant in sun angle for every species, so the kernel SHAPE is right and only the LEVEL is species-dependent - driving those to 1.00 wants a per-species scalar baked into the billboard atlas, which is named as the follow-up rather than hidden.

recent_decisions.decision: CLOUD REPRESENTATION SURVEY (wf_2d50711f-41d) - THE DIRECTION FINDING. No shipped AAA cloud system builds cumulus BODIES out of noise. Every modern one uses noise ONLY as erosion applied to a shape that came from somewhere else. Nubis3 (SIGGRAPH 2023) is explicit: the body is an authored 8 m Dimensional Profile voxel field and the 128^3 noise is applied as ValueErosion(dimensional_profile, noise_composite) to up-rez it to 0.5 m. HumanityOS has this wiring INVERTED - inverted Worley IS our body - which is precisely the operator uniform spheres complaint. Worley cells are also near-UNIFORM in size, so the representation is structurally incapable of the POWER-LAW size distribution real cumulus fields have. SECOND FINDING, independent and immediately actionable: Nubis3 sphere-traces an SDF, step = max(sdf_distance, max(1.0, sqrt(cam_dist)*0.08)) + jitter, giving an 8 m floor at 10 km; Guerrilla measured that swap as 6.1-8.2 ms -> 2.2-4.0 ms, i.e. BETTER AND FASTER. Calibration that settles our march debate: even 2017-era 2.5D Nubis stepped 3 m near / 63 m at 16 km - our 775 m average is ~12x coarser than a nine-year-old technique. WHAT DOES NOT FIT US: Nubis3 NVDF storage as shipped (25.166 MB buys 16 km^2; tiling a 200x200 km fly-through region is ~63 GB, needs an artist, cannot be MODIS-driven).
